notes: Maximizing is now Nova's own: the window fills the work area and remembers its old size. Dragging the tab row out of a maximized window, or out of full screen, brings out a smaller window that follows the mouse, also onto another screen.
The maximize button and a double click on the tab row use the same maximize.
The shortcut and icon repair now keys on the version Nova really runs, so it applies again after each update.
Dragging the tab row while the window is maximized or in full screen now brings out a smaller window that follows the mouse, also onto another screen.
The address bar has the same gap to the tabs above and to the bookmarks below.
Settings are laid out as a sheet: the title of each section stands in a column of its own with a small accent mark, its switches beside it.
A new icon identity and icon files for the taskbar, the Start menu and the desktop shortcut: Nova repairs its own shortcuts once after this update.
The Nova crystal is back in the toolbar, at the far left before the back button.
The left and right sides of the toolbar keep a little more room in narrow windows, so the address bar stays centred.

headline.title: Tabs like in Brave
headline.text: tabs along the top from the far left, the address bar centred below, bookmarks underneath, window buttons top right.

notes: Tabs are clearly separated and the numbers (memory, blocked ads, tab budget) are small and quiet beside the buttons.
One Extensions button opens a small list; click an extension to open its own menu.
Bookmark star left of the address bar: click it to name the page, save it or take it out again.
Spaces moved out of the tab row into a small button with a list.

Drag a tab out of the tab row (also onto another screen) and a complete second Nova opens with the same tabs, bars and options. Ctrl+N opens a new window, and a tab can be moved between windows from the tab menu.
Drag the empty part of the tab row to move the window; from full size it comes out smaller under the cursor.
Settings look plainer: text menu, simple lists, no icon tiles.
Less work in the background: the interface gets rarely changing data only when it changed, blocked ads no longer refresh everything, memory figure updates only when it moved.
If Nova ever closes unexpectedly it now writes a short log and a crash report for you in the Nova data folder.

headline.title: A fresh start for Nova
headline.text: a new logo, a start page where your most visited sites orbit the search, downloads that live in the sidebar and settings that sit right beside your browser.

notes: Drag a tab out of the tab list into a window of its own, or choose Move to new window in the tab menu. Back to Nova puts it back.
A middle click or Ctrl+click on a link opens it in a background tab, and you stay where you are.
Downloads: a tray in the sidebar with progress, speed and time left, and a progress ring on the download button.
Settings sit beside the browser, so every change shows live. New Built in page for the tools that replace extensions.
Websites follow Windows, Light or Dark: decides whether sites with a dark theme of their own use it.
The extension hub has a way back to Settings and an Installed view.
Tab overview and library redesigned.
A calmer update screen with the main feature of each release first.
The dock is tidier: stats on top, buttons below.
Settings rebuilt: clearer pages, feature cards, and a docked panel that leaves your sidebar visible so every change shows live.
Layout page now holds the sidebar arrangement: move parts up and down, hide the ones you do not use.
Download button next to reload with a progress ring and a panel for all downloads: speed, time left, pause, resume, cancel, open.
Extension hub opens straight from Settings and from a button in the dock, with an Installed view.
Tab overview and library redesigned.
New logo and icons, and a new animated Setup with a supernova.
This update screen: logo, version and what is new after every update.
Built-in password saver (optional, off by default): saves and fills logins with encrypted storage, CSV import and export.
Dragging the window out of full screen now restores a smaller window under the pointer.
Setup assistant offers the built-in tools instead of extensions.
Faster downloads: big files come down over up to 8 connections at once, with pause, resume and continue after a restart.
Disk cache limit with automatic cleaning, under Settings > Performance.
Float video when you switch tabs.
Colours from your wallpaper and the Windows accent colour.
Layout editor: reorder and hide the parts of the sidebar.
Built in instead of extensions, all off by default: video speed keys, SponsorBlock, YouTube dislike count and cookie banner hiding.
A new Setup window with an animated look.
